title: Chocolate chip cookies
skill: Creaming butter and sugar; even scoops

move.title: Cream it, scoop it even
move.body: Chocolate chip cookies start by creaming: beating soft butter with sugar until it turns pale and fluffy. Today you'll cream by hand, scoop the dough into even balls, and space them on the pan so every cookie bakes the same.

callback.body: Brown butter cookies melt and brown the butter first. These keep the butter soft and beat air into it with the sugar, for a puffier, softer cookie.

why.title: Why cream
why.body: Beating soft butter with sugar pushes tiny air bubbles into the butter. The bubbles grow in the oven, so the cookies puff and stay soft.

why.title: Soft, not melted
why.body: Soft butter holds air when you beat it. Melted butter can't, and the cookies spread flat. It's ready when a finger pressed in leaves a dent.

why.title: Even scoops
why.body: Cookies the same size bake in the same time. Small ones burn while big ones are still raw. A tablespoon makes every ball the same.

why.title: Room to spread
why.body: Cookies spread as the butter melts. Two inches between balls keeps them from baking into each other.

wrong.sign: The cookies spread flat and thin
wrong.fix: The butter was too warm or melted. Chill the dough 15 minutes before the next pan.

wrong.sign: Some cookies burned and some are raw
wrong.fix: They weren't the same size. Use the tablespoon for every ball.
Space them 2 inches apart, 12 to a pan.
They baked too long. Take them out while the middles still look soft.

quiz.explain: The air bubbles make cookies puff.

quiz.q: Why scoop every cookie with the same spoon?
choices: So they all bake in the same time
quiz.explain: Small ones burn while big ones are raw.
They firm up as they cool.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 375°F. Line the sheet pan with parchment.
steps.tip: Take the butter out of the fridge an hour before you start.

steps.text: Beat the soft butter, brown sugar, and sugar in the large bowl with the wooden spoon.
Add the egg and vanilla. Beat until smooth.
Wash your hands with soap, and throw away the eggshell.
Spoon and level the flour into the medium bowl. Whisk in the baking soda and salt.
steps.tip: Don't scoop with the cup. It packs in too much flour.

steps.text: Stir the flour into the butter just until no flour shows. Stir in the chocolate chips.
steps.look: A soft dough with chips all through.
steps.tip: Don't taste the raw dough. It has raw egg and flour.

steps.text: Scoop level tablespoons of dough and roll them into balls. Set 12 on the pan, 2 inches apart.
steps.look: Four rows of three, all the same size.

steps.text: Bake until the edges are golden.
steps.look: Golden edges, and the middles look soft.

steps.text: With an adult and oven mitts, take out the pan. Look at the edges and the middles.

target.look: Golden edges and soft, puffy middles

steps.text: Let them cool on the pan for 5 minutes, then move them to the rack with the spatula.
steps.tip: They firm up as they cool.

steps.text: Let the pan cool, then scoop and bake the rest the same way. Turn off the oven at the end.
steps.look: About 24 cookies, all the same size.
